beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. Your line held better than most I have seen since the first war. Come find me for a drink sometime.
{player} took the field today with {troop_count} troops and a clear plan. I respect that. The fen is yours for now.
Ser {player}, that was a clean victory. Do not let it go to your head. My ledger has a line for you now, and it is written in ink.
{player}, you have bested me, and I will not pretend otherwise. My ledger still lists that fen as mine, and I am patient enough to wait for the rematch.
Your {gold} gold in tribute was fair, {player}. Keep the coin and keep your men fed. Hunger has ended more campaigns than any blade.

beat_by_player.text: That fen was closer than the scouts claimed, {player}. You fought well with {troop_count} men. Shall we tally the losses at the inn?
Ser {player}, you have nothing to be ashamed of. A cold plan beats many a brave man. Regroup and return with fuller ranks.
Good fight, {player}. You held your flank longer than most veterans of the first war would have. Keep your banners high and your rear covered next time.
I won today, {player}, but my ledger notes you made me work for it. Do not expect that fen back without a fight.
{player}, that was a fair win for me, and you know it. Bring {troop_count} more and we will see whether the ledger changes.

fought_alongside_player.text: Well done holding the line against {enemy_faction}, {player}. {troop_count} men and not one of them broke. That is a good field.
We held the ford together, {player}. I have not seen a shield wall that tidy since the first war. Keep your flank close and we will keep winning.
Ser {player}, your timing against {enemy_faction} was sharp. Remember that day. Good allies are scarcer than good fens.
Fine work alongside you today, {player}. The {enemy_faction} banners will remember that field for a while.
Thank you for covering my right, {player}. I owe you a meal and a tip about grain stores that you will not find in any book.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me walk free and asked for no coin. My ledger has rarely recorded a kindness so plainly. I will not forget it.
{player} released me instead of ransoming me. That is a rare thing on this continent. Good on you, and thank you.
Released by {player} without ransom. I will note it in the ledger and keep my own counsel on the rest of it.
You let me go, {player}, and I will not owe you for it. Still, I remember the face. Our account is not closed yet.
{player} let me go without ransom. Fine. A rival who spares captives is still a rival, and I still expect a rematch.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. The old fens remember every oath, and yours is now part of that record. Ask me anything.
Ser {player}, I am glad to have you under the banner of {my_faction}. Come to me for the old routes and honest prices.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Let us see whether the oath holds through the next winter. Most do not.
Welcome, {player}. I have read a great many oaths in my time. Keep yours and I will think better of you than most.
I do not trust a sudden change of banner, {player}. Prove the oath with blood before I call you one of us.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} is in good hands now, {player}. The garrison there will be lucky to have a commander who counts the grain.
Ser {player}, congratulations on {fief}. Walk its walls before you sleep. The ones who know a fortress by its stones rule it best.
{player} now holds {fief}. I have held worse and kept my head, so the ruler's choice is not mine to question today.
{fief} is yours now, {player}. Enjoy the honor, and do not forget the men who won it for you.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Pardon my thin smile. I held that wall longer than you have been on this server.

encounter_greeting.text: Well met, {player}. This is {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have a fresh pot of advice if your men need some. Come share a fire.
{player}, our paths cross again. Walk with care past the ford ahead. The rain has been heavy, and the mud there has swallowed better riders.
{player}, I see your banners. I have not forgotten the last field between us. Keep your distance and we will both live to see the next one.
Good to see you on the road, {player}. Stop with us a while. I can tell you where the grain is cheapest between here and the coast.
Greetings, {player}. Mind the crossing to the west. My scouts report a patrol there that does not care for strangers.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, {player}. Keep your water full and your horses rested. The road is long, and the good ones are never in a hurry.
We part here, {player}. Fair roads to you. I will see you at the next crossing, whichever banner you march under.
Go on then, {player}. I have a long memory and a short temper for those who run from a fair field.
Farewell, {player}. Remember what I said about the ford, and send word if you need a hand. I am rarely far from the road.
Keep moving, {player}. Next time we meet I will expect better than the last, and so will my ledger.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain around {town} has turned the roads to soup again. Anyone hauling grain east should wait for a dry week.
I passed through {village} this morning. The well is still clean and the children still chase geese. Some things do not change.
Every veteran here should remember the first war. Half of you were not born yet, and the other half forgot the marsh shortcut.
Heard a wagon train from {town} got lost in the fog. If anyone is near the old causeway, pull them out. It costs nothing.
Hael_Stackbane still has not answered my challenge. I am a patient man, but the ledger has started to complain.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost most of their army today, and I have seen this before. Pick up what is left and march home. The fen will still be there.
Ser {player}, I heard about the {troop_count} men you lost. A bad day does not make a bad commander. Eat, rest, and count again.
Your losses were heavy, {player}. Sit with me when you can and I will show you where the last three commanders went wrong.
Rough field for {player} today. Every veteran has been crushed once. The ones who last are those who come back.
{player} got overrun today, and I will not gloat about it. My ledger has no room for that kind of pleasure.
